title: Instantiating a self-referencing class leaks its GDScript at exit when an unrelated loaded script upcasts a derived class in a typed return
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in: v4.6.stable.official [89cea1439], v4.6.3.stable.official [7d41c59c4], v4.7.1.stable.official [a13da4feb] (latest stable at the time of writing)

### System information

Windows 11 Pro (build 26200) - official win64 builds, run from the CLI with `--headless` (dummy rendering/display driver)

### Issue description

Creating one instance of a GDScript class leaks that class's `GDScript` resource (plus a `GDScriptNativeClass`) at exit — but only when a second, textually unrelated script is loaded in the same process. The interaction needs three ingredients at once, and removing any one of them makes the leak disappear. All scripts involved are trivial; two of the load-bearing functions are never called, and the second script is never instantiated.

With the 5-script MRP below:

```text
$ godot --headless --path . -s res://probe.gd
p=true ref=true
WARNING: ObjectDB instances leaked at exit (run with --verbose for details).
ERROR: 1 resources still in use at exit (run with --verbose for details).
```

`--verbose` names them:

```text
Leaked instance: GDScriptNativeClass:9223372052742800278 - Reference count: 1
Leaked instance: GDScript:9223372063362778560 - Reference count: 1
Resource still in use: res://plan.gd (GDScript)
```

Note that the leaked script is `plan.gd` — a script that `label.gd`, `sink.gd`, and `canvas_sink.gd` never mention, and whose only living instance was dropped on the same line it was created.

Each row below is a single change applied to the MRP as given (verified on 4.6.stable; the unmodified MRP itself was verified on 4.6, 4.6.3, and 4.7.1):

| Single change from the MRP | Result |
|---|---|
| none (MRP as-is) | **leaks** (`plan.gd` + `GDScriptNativeClass`) |
| `probe.gd`: remove the `preload("res://label.gd")` | no leak |
| `probe.gd`: remove the `Plan.new()` call | no leak |
| `plan.gd`: delete `build()` entirely | no leak |
| `plan.gd`: untyped return `static func build():` (body still `return Plan.new()`) | **leaks** |
| `label.gd`: declare the return as the derived type `-> CanvasSink` | no leak |
| `label.gd`: explicit base type `var s: Sink = CanvasSink.new()` | **leaks** |
| `label.gd`: `return CanvasSink.new()` directly, no local | **leaks** |
| `canvas_sink.gd`: delete `create()` entirely | no leak |

So the three required ingredients seem to be:

1. `plan.gd` contains a self-reference (a static factory whose body or return type names its own class — the annotation alone is not what matters, since the untyped-return variant still leaks) **and** one instance of `Plan` is actually created at runtime. The factory itself is never called.
2. `label.gd` is loaded (only `preload`, never instantiated, its method never called) and contains a method whose **declared return type is a base user class while the body returns a derived instance** (`-> Sink` returning a `CanvasSink`). Declaring the true derived type instead avoids the leak.
3. The derived class `canvas_sink.gd` itself contains a never-called self-referencing static factory.

The leak scales with project size. In our real project (~130 scripts) one such naturally-occurring pair leaks 10 script resources from a plain `-s` run; a synthetic version of this MRP cloned 60× leaks 178 resources.

Possibly related: #71898 (3.x, self-referencing static factory leaks the script — the shape of ingredient 1 in isolation, which on 4.6/4.7 is clean until combined with ingredient 2).

**Crash escalation on 4.6.0 (fixed in later patches, included for context):** in our full project's test runs (gdUnit4, ~1000 tests, all passing) the same leak class escalated on v4.6.stable to a segfault **during engine teardown**, after the test runner had printed its complete green report and "Finallize .. done" — process exit 139 with 108 leaked script resources. The identical run under 4.6.3 leaks identically but exits 0, and Linux CI always exited 0, so current stables appear to only leak where 4.6.0 crashed at shutdown. Same crash class as the closed #43529, #69183, #84327. I can file details of that crash separately if useful, but since 4.6.3+ no longer crashes, this report is about the leak that seeded it.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create an empty folder containing the 6 files below (`project.godot` + 5 scripts).
2. `godot --headless --import --path .`
3. `godot --headless --path . -s res://probe.gd`

Expected: clean exit with no leak errors (nothing outlives the run: the only created instance is dropped immediately, nothing else is instantiated or called).
Actual: `plan.gd` and a `GDScriptNativeClass` are reported leaked at exit, every run.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

All 6 files inline (text only — happy to attach a zip if preferred):

`project.godot`:
```ini
config_version=5

[application]
config/name="script-leak-mrp"
```

`plan.gd`:
```gdscript
class_name Plan
extends RefCounted


static func build() -> Plan:
	return Plan.new()
```

`sink.gd`:
```gdscript
class_name Sink
extends RefCounted
```

`canvas_sink.gd`:
```gdscript
class_name CanvasSink
extends Sink


static func create() -> CanvasSink:
	return CanvasSink.new()
```

`label.gd`:
```gdscript
extends Control


func _resolve_sink() -> Sink:
	var s := CanvasSink.new()
	return s
```

`probe.gd`:
```gdscript
extends SceneTree

const LabelScript := preload("res://label.gd")


func _initialize() -> void:
	var p := Plan.new()
	print("p=", p != null, " ref=", LabelScript != null)
	quit(0)
```
